**Yes.** The contract allows termination for convenience by either party, which includes the customer, on **at least 60 days' written notice**.

**Section 31:**
> "Either party may terminate this agreement for convenience by giving not less than sixty (60) days' written notice."

**Points to note:**

- **"Not less than" sets a minimum.** The customer can give more than 60 days' notice but not less.
- **Notice must be in writing.** Check the master agreement for notice formalities, such as delivery method and addresses.
- **The document may be incomplete or combined.** The numbering restarts at Section 1 after Section 31, and the second series (Sections 1–25) covers "Definitions and interpretation." This suggests the text may be two documents joined together, or that a schedule or part is missing. Confirm which document Section 31 belongs to and whether it governs your relationship.
- **The master agreement matters.** Nearly every section defers to a master agreement that isn't included here. It may contain terms that affect this right, such as termination fees, minimum commitment periods, payment for work performed up to termination, or an order-of-precedence clause that decides which document wins in a conflict. Review it before relying on Section 31.
